questions.question: It is illegal to ride a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In California, riders age 21 and older cannot ride with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Riders under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Riding with any alcohol in your system is not safe.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip over. Use only the rear brake to slow down during the U-turn.

questions.question: When choosing a jacket for protection, make sure it:

options.text: Fits loosely and flaps in the wind.
Fits snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Is not made of leather or other sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose a jacket and pants made of leather or other sturdy material. They should fit snugly enough that they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should stay at least this far behind the vehicle ahead:
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance behind other vehicles under normal conditions. When conditions are not perfect, increase your following distance.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation teaches the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does SEE stand for?
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions while riding. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: Which factor can affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the drinker's body weight.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: To keep your high beam headlight turned on.
To paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep your high beam headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on day and night. Use your high beam whenever it is legal and safe to do so.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for passengers. Good footing helps prevent your passenger from falling off the bike.

questions.question: When riding at night, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead when riding at night.

questions.question: When stopping with a passenger on your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than normal
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes your motorcycle slower to respond. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier when you have a passenger, go slower overall, and look for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: To help others see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in low visibility
Add an orange tint to your headlight

questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on at all times.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close together while having enough space. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding on curves, or entering or leaving a road.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle at night, how can you tell if there are bumps in the road ahead?

options.text: Listen for the vehicle scraping the pavement
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down
Look at the rear bumper to see if it is bouncing

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down
questions.explanation: Use the vehicle ahead to learn about road conditions at night. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps in the road ahead.

questions.question: Before riding, check your clutch. A working clutch should feel:
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, move to a different lane to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time than usual to stop and speed up
The same amount of time to stop and speed up
More time than usual to stop and speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: More time than usual to stop and speed up
questions.explanation: Extra weight makes a motorcycle slower to accelerate and decelerate. Your motorcycle responds more slowly when carrying a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: Which is NOT a method to maintain control when turning?
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle in a turn, slow down before entering it. Look where you want to go. Press the handle grip to lean in the right direction. Gently speed up through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: To be more visible to other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you. This works any time of day.

questions.question: A main cause of single-motorcycle crashes is:

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve.
Running off the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve.
questions.explanation: Taking a curve too wide is a main cause of single-motorcycle crashes. This can cause the motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, during a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: Using both brakes:

options.text: Should be done every time you stop.
Should only be done in an emergency.
Should only be done on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done every time you stop.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Do not wait for an emergency.

questions.question: Eye protection:

options.text: Is not needed if your motorcycle has a windshield.
Is only needed in bad weather.
Should let you see clearly to the sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should let you see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required by law in California. A face shield can protect your whole face during a crash. Good eye or face protection must let you see clearly to both sides.
